notes: The page begins in continuation with passage aux complémentaires) and relates the ten triangles of I to the ten faces of the icosaèdre gauche, also described in the manuscript as pairs of opposite faces of the ordinary icosahedron. M1051 remains an uncertain correspondant/correspondent; the adjective gauche is legible in all three occurrences on this page. The geometric identification is a manuscript claim, not a result proved in this reading.

The manuscript describes the fifteen partitions of type (2,2,1) of I as square structures on four of its five points, with the two pairs taken from diagonally opposite vertices. It says these correspond to the fifteen edges of the same skew icosahedron. The upper drawing has four filled vertices, two smaller marks on opposite sides, and a detached right-hand point. These are source statements and depicted features; no geometric reconstruction of the polyhedron was attempted.

The slanted NB note assigns to a side a the colors of the four other sides of the adjacent faces, grouped into two pairs. Two distinct canceled low words, both tentatively deux, are present where C recorded only one. The far-right en and the final des deux faces retain attachment/reading uncertainty. The diamond below has separate f and a labels and an upper gap in its vertical stroke; the gap is represented without a topological inference.

The revised incidence passage links an edge a and a face f through the triangle and square assigned to them. The inserted reformulation says that the complement of the triangle is one of the two pairs defining the square. The manuscript then compares the incidence relation of its literal diviseurs à sommets of the structure hat M_{0,I} with faces and edges of the skew icosahedron, or dually vertices and edges of the dodecahedron. The old deux may be canceled or may remain under an insertion connector, and the written numeral 2 remains afterward; neither the wording nor the moduli interpretation has been silently corrected or proved.

Finite computation performed after the visual reading: on an explicitly constructed five-element set, enumeration gives 10 three-element subsets and 15 unordered partitions with two pairs and one singleton. Under the written criterion that the triangle complement equal one of the pairs, each partition is incident with 2 triangles, each triangle with 3 partitions, and there are 30 incidences. The same counts follow from binomial(5,3)=10 and 5*3=15. This verifies the finite counts and that combinatorial incidence criterion only; it does not prove the claimed polyhedral or moduli identifications, and it was not used to choose doubtful letters.

The straight underline immediately below incident is separate from its lower curved connector and has been restored. The first diagram's lower small point is placed on its edge, and the second diagram's divider stops short of the upper vertex. In the NB note no separate final period is visible after faces. The mark after correspond remains à|:. Eight definite canceled spans plus the possible cancellation of main-text deux are inventoried; the two alternative TeX branches describe one physical l'un des insertion, not two. Nine physical main-text insertions are represented, with the separately doubtful en placement in the margin.

Physical reading count is 38: 21 principal prose rows, 7 slanted NB rows, 8 interlinear annotation baselines (one band for a/(incident)/f, one for l'un des, one for opposés, two for the long i.e. sentence, two for Donc on voit que, and one for the paired final replacements), one baseline for f and a inside the margin drawing, and the pencil-foliation row. Unlabeled drawing geometry is inventoried separately rather than counted as a prose line. Full scan and both native halves were each viewed once; all 16 saved crops were viewed individually, with crop06 rotated -30 degrees. There are 41 substantive comparison rows and 13 second-reading boxes; overlapping boxes account for steeply slanted lines and interlinear material without inventing text from clipped neighboring context.

No own ink page number appears at the top; 66 is separate pencil foliation whose hand is not confidently attributed. Only M1051, M1052 and M1053 occur in decisions, in that order. M1053 is resolved to sommets; the reordering of the same two candidates at M1051 is not counted as a substantive C correction. Certainty-only additions for en, the state of deux and à|: are recorded as doubts, while any actual H word or placement difference remains in changes.

No OCR, outside research, TeX compilation or other page was used. The finite enumeration in N5 is the only mathematical computation performed here. The source's words, crossed states, apparent slips, abbreviations and locally reduced punctuation remain separate from the unproved mathematical identifications.
